title: Permission oracle fixtures and audit-replay test harness
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a resilient, reproducible test harness for RBAC v2 permission assertions that combines canonical fixture snapshots (permission oracles) with an audit-log replay engine. This ticket covers the fixture schema, deterministic synthetic principal generator, replay orchestration, and CI integration so nightly runs detect regressions in permission decisions, SSO/SAML admin edge-cases, and audit logging fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic fixture format (JSONL) produced from real production-like states that captures principals, resources, actions, role bindings, and evaluation context
A replay harness that can consume a fixture and assert the current RBAC v2 engine returns the expected allow/deny decision and emits an audit event matching a schema
Correlation of replay assertions with audit-log entries (timestamp tolerant) and a failure report that highlights policy drift and missing audit fields
Nightly CI job that runs the suite on runtime-1.22 images and uploads a pass/fail matrix to the Console dashboard
Performance budget: full suite <= 30 minutes in CI with smart sampling; incremental runs <= 7 minutes for changed modules
Security review completed and KMS key usage for any sensitive fixture material confirmed
implementation_notes: Fixture design: compact JSONL lines where each record contains: id, principal{type,id,attributes}, resource{type,id,labels}, action, environment, expected_decision, expected_audit_fields
Synthetic principal generator will use realistic attribute distributions (org size, nested groups, service-accounts) to surface edge cases such as nested role inheritance and cross-tenant bindings
Replay engine will run both unit-mode (fast isolated logic checks) and integrated-mode (through the full authorization GRPC path) to catch translation bugs
Audit correlation will allow +/- 5s timestamp drift and match by trace_id when available; fallback matching by principal+action+resource
Storage of fixtures in an immutable S3 prefix with versioned keys and an index file mapping fixture sets to production dates and source PRs
CI integration: GitHub Actions job matrix that spins up a lightweight runtime container built from runtime-1.22 commit, runs the harness, and publishes results to /console/tests/rbac-oracles
Failure triage: generate a reproducible minimal fixture per failing assertion and attach to the GH check with a suggested owner tag based on policy namespace
progress_updates: 2026-01-20: Spike completed comparing three fixture schemas; chose JSONL for line-delimited diffs and streaming

2026-02-05: Audit correlation logic implemented; added trace_id matching and timestamp tolerance. Early runs show missing principal_email field in 3 audit event types — opened ENG-33210 to fix logging shim

tradeoffs_and_decisions: Snapshot granularity vs maintenance: decided on smaller, focused fixture sets (per-namespace and per-role-template) rather than monolithic dumps to reduce churn and make diffs actionable
Deterministic vs probabilistic tests: core assertions are deterministic; separate fuzz suite will run probabilistic workloads nightly to explore state-space without blocking PRs
Audit fidelity matching rules: chosen conservative matching (trace_id preferred) to avoid false positives when multiple similar events occur in high-throughput tests
Storage: use versioned S3 to simplify rollbacks rather than DB-backed fixtures to avoid migration complexity
